## Body

- **Memory turn (F130, #184).** On compact or close it covers this context's holdings: the open ones plus those released after the cutoff, newest first, 32 max, and the prompt says when there were more.
  - The cutoff is the admitted_at of the newest compact plan 222 settled as delivered (woken/resumed/holds-nothing) among the seat's 16 newest compaction_wakes rows, via migration 0045's indexes.
  - With no delivered compact recorded, every release counts. That fallback only adds to the prompt.
  - A store error or a lookup over 2 s takes a generic turn: a brake, never a refusal (refusing a compact can strand a full seat).
  - Names go through [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}. Released ones show "released HH:MM" in local time.
- **Compact jobs** are kind delivery:<seat> for most seats and delivery-control:<seat> for Copilot. A done job doesn't mean the compact ran: refused ones are acked done.
- **Copilot receiver (F124, #180).** canRetryDiscarded reads the native queue and processing state before the gap uncertainty, so a still-queued steer waits.
  - An uncertain discard never resends. It waits for up to HOLD_ESCALATION_MS with heartbeats running (discard-uncertain), then holds.
  - A hard hold (holdReceiving) still stops heartbeats, so the lease lapses and the PA digest shows receiver-lapsed. No test pins the heartbeat stop (bobcat's note).
  - The progress.test.mjs replay of the 12:31 ids is the regression proof.
- **Diagnosis order** that worked every time: the extension log (~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log, receive-held / receiver-rebaselined lines), then the seat's session events.jsonl for timing, then the store (jobs, spine, compaction_wakes, community_assignments), and only then the code.
